chicago-4d-smoke.yml.trigger_prefix:
name: Chicago 4D — full smoke

# The renderer smoke on a runner WITHOUT the per-command ceiling.
#
# ROADMAP § THE RUN BUDGET, and T-0060: a steward run's single foreground
# command is capped at ten minutes, and by 2026-08-18 neither viewport's full
# unfiltered pass fit inside it. Steward runs verify with SMOKE_STAGE parts
# (each fits a command); THIS workflow is where an unfiltered pass lives — the
# reference measurement the halves are audited against, and the only place the
# whole gate runs as one process. Dispatch it on any ref, e.g.:
#
#   gh workflow run chicago-4d-smoke.yml --ref <branch> -f viewport=mobile
#
# It is dispatch-plus-one-path on purpose. The dev gate (chicago-4d-check.yml)
# stays ~90 s and advisory speed matters there; a ~25-minute-per-viewport
# Playwright crawl on every push would be a queue, not a gate (one path is not
# a queue). The nightly bake already smokes the mirror it publishes.
# The single push path self-tests workflow edits once they land on dev (T-3121).
# Merging that edit into a PR branch must not launch another full measurement on
# its head and leave its normal gate waiting for the 150-minute timeout.
# Explicit dispatch is unchanged; GitHub requires the workflow to be registered
# on the default branch. Empty inputs still run both viewports and every part.

on:
  push:
    branches: [dev]
    paths:
      - '.github/workflows/chicago-4d-smoke.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      viewport:
        description: 'SMOKE_VIEWPORT — empty for both, or mobile / desktop'
        required: false
        default: ''
      stage:
        description: 'SMOKE_STAGE — empty for the full body, or a part 1..15 / a range like 3-4'
        required: false
        default: ''

chicago-4d-check.yml.trigger_prefix:
name: Chicago 4D — gate

# The fast half of the two-speed build: schema, provenance, date gates,
# referential integrity, licences, staleness, datum re-derivation, JS parse.
# Seconds, and no Blender — the content build lives in chicago-4d-bake.yml.
#
# THIS IS THE DEV GATE (chicago/4d/docs/PIPELINE.md). It runs on PRs INTO dev and
# on pushes TO dev. Merging into dev is STAGE, not ship — it publishes only the
# /4d/dev/ preview, and production moves only when the owner dispatches
# chicago-4d-promote-to-prod.yml.
#
# THE PUSH TRIGGER IS FILTERED TO dev AND main, AND THE COMMENT THAT USED TO STAND
# HERE SAID NOT TO DO THAT (T-1288). It said an unfiltered push trigger was
# deliberate, "so nobody tidies it into `branches: [main]`", because the gate has to
# cover steward branches too. That reason is real and it is already served by the
# `pull_request` trigger; what the unfiltered push actually bought was a SECOND,
# IDENTICAL RUN.
#
# A steward branch with an open pull request satisfies BOTH triggers, so every push
# to it started this 439-step suite TWICE on the same commit. Measured 2026-09-17 on
# every open PR in the queue at once — #1413, #1412, #1411, #1409, #1405 and #1392
# each carried two `gate` check runs on one head sha.
#
# AND IT IS NOT ONLY WASTE. A pull request is not `clean` until every required check
# has passed, so the PR waited on the SLOWER of two identical runs. That was
# observed directly: four PRs sat `blocked` with one gate green and its twin still
# in progress. The duplicate was doubling time-to-mergeable, and the lap re-pushes
# every open PR on every merge into dev, so the cost was paid once per PR PER LAP —
# four laps in the hour this was found.
#
# WHAT THE FILTER GIVES UP, stated rather than glossed: a steward branch pushed
# BEFORE its pull request exists is not gated by that push. The gap closes the
# moment the PR opens, which in this repo is the same run — and a run that dies
# before opening one now gets a DRAFT PR from the steward's salvage step (T-1155),
# which fires `pull_request` and gates it. Nothing that was covered stops being
# covered; only the second copy goes.
# AND IT MUST RUN ON A WORKFLOW-ONLY CHANGE, or such a change can never merge.
# `gate` is a REQUIRED check on dev. A pull request that touches only
# .github/workflows/ produced no gate run at all, so the requirement could never be
# satisfied and the PR sat `blocked` for ever. Found on #1433 — the fix for an
# eleven-hour production deploy outage, which changes deploy.yml and
# chicago-4d-promote-to-prod.yml and nothing else, and was therefore unmergeable by
# construction. The paths below now cover the whole workflow directory rather than
# this one file. A workflow edit is rare and consequential, and check.sh already
# holds assertions about these files, so paying the gate for one is right.
on:
  push:
    branches: [dev, main]
    paths:
      - 'chicago/4d/**'
      - 'chicago/reference/**'
      - '.github/workflows/**'
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'chicago/4d/**'
      - 'chicago/reference/**'
      - '.github/workflows/**'
  workflow_dispatch:

chicago-4d-moving-frames.yml.trigger_prefix:
name: Chicago 4D — moving frames

# T-2106. THE MOVING-FRAME GATE, IN A CI LEG OF ITS OWN.
#
# The owner's report (2026-10-04) was that walking lagged, and every frame budget
# this project held was read at a STAND. tools/measure_walk_frames.mjs drives a
# walk, a turn in place, a flight and a ride frame by frame and times what flora
# spends in each; `--gate` holds the worst frame and the p95 per tier to the
# ceilings written in that file, and `--verify` checks that a rebuild spread over
# frames lands exactly the plants a one-frame rebuild deals. Until this leg the
# gate only ran when a steward run thought to run it.
#
# It is NOT in check.sh, and NOT in the dev gate's `gate` job, because it is a
# browser run of about seven minutes: the dev gate is the window in which a PR can
# be overtaken, and it does not get longer for one family of files. It runs beside
# it, on the pull requests that can move a moving frame: the renderer's own
# JavaScript, the flora and tree data it plants from, and this tool.
#
# Desktop only, unthrottled. The phone stand-in reads the same code under a 4x CPU
# throttle somebody chose; the desktop reading is the one on this runner that is
# not scaled by a factor, which is why the ceilings are written against it.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'chicago/4d/renderers/web/js/**'
      - 'chicago/4d/data/flora/**'
      - 'chicago/4d/tools/measure_walk_frames.mjs'
      - 'chicago/4d/tools/check_upload_release.mjs'
      - '.github/workflows/chicago-4d-moving-frames.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:
